title: Khuzaymah Bin Bishr and Ikrimah Al-Fayyaz

keywords: khuzaymah bin bishr and ikrimah al-fayyaz
full_text:
Khuzaymah bin Bishr was an affluent and generous nobleman of the province of Mesopotamia who squandered his fortune feeding travelers and relieving the debts of the poor until he was reduced to total ruin. His former companions abandoned him, and he locked his doors, preparing to starve with his family in dignified silence.

The governor of the province, Ikrimah al-Fayyaz—whose title meant 'The Overflowing in Generosity'—heard of Khuzaymah’s distress.

Ikrimah did not wish to humiliate the proud nobleman with a public donation. In the dead of night, disguised in a rough woolen cloak, the governor rode alone to Khuzaymah’s house, knocked on the door, and placed four heavy sacks containing four thousand gold dinars upon the threshold.

Khuzaymah seized the stranger’s cloak, demanding: 'Who are you, noble benefactor, that heaven has sent to save my children?'

The stranger replied: 'I am Ghiyath al-Mustaghithin—The Succor of Those Who Call for Help!' and vanished into the darkness.

Khuzaymah paid his debts, bought new estates, and prospered. Later, traveling to Damascus, he was received by the Caliph Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, who appointed him Governor of Mesopotamia.

When Khuzaymah arrived to take command, he audited the provincial accounts and found a deficit in Ikrimah’s ledger—for Ikrimah had spent his own wealth on the poor! Khuzaymah, not recognizing his secret benefactor, placed Ikrimah in prison according to strict law.

Ikrimah’s wife visited Khuzaymah in secret and revealed the truth: 'The man you have imprisoned is Ghiyath al-Mustaghithin!'

Khuzaymah turned pale with horror! He ran to the prison, struck off the chains with his own hands, threw himself at Ikrimah’s feet, and wept bitter tears of remorse.

He took Ikrimah to Damascus, where the Caliph rewarded both noble men with royal honors, praising a friendship built on selfless secret charity.
moral: Secret charity done for the sake of virtue creates an unbreakable bond that elevates noble men.
